newsitem.title: UK: UK firm seeks end of EU aluminium import tariff.
newsitem.headline: UK firm seeks end of EU aluminium import tariff.

text.p: The six percent import tariff on aluminium into the European Union (EU) should be debated at the World Trade Organisation (WTO) meeting in Singapore in December, with British Alcan Aluminium plc, a subsidiary of Alcan Aluminium Ltd, calling for its elimination.

Although a majority of primary aluminium producers in Europe recommend that the tariff should be retained the EU is the only major trading bloc to maintain a tariff against aluminium, British Alcan said in a briefing paper.
"U.S., Canada and Japan have all recognised the competive advantage for their aluminium industries by eliminating duty on primary metal," British Alcan said.
The EU depends on a growing level of imported aluminium to meet demand growth from fabricating, and as primary production cannot be increased the Union has to rely on rising imports.

"The six-percent levy introduces a substantial distortion of trade. Despite the duty, at least 40 percent of imported metal enters the EU duty free under either EFTA or LOME Convention arrangements," it said.
Continuing the duty will penalise Europe's manufacturing industry and is against the interest of most of those employed in the aluminium industry, British Alcan said.
